items.title: Being proper over the base descends along an fpqc covering
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes of locally finite type, a closed subset Z of the source is proper over the base as soon as its inverse image in the base change along some fpqc covering is (statement lines 6726-6734). The proof begins with a choice that makes the rest work: Z is endowed with the reduced induced closed subscheme structure, which is what turns a statement about a closed subset into a statement about a morphism of schemes (proof lines 6737-6738). For each member of the covering, the base change of Z is identified as a closed subscheme of the base changed source whose underlying closed subset is the given inverse image, and the definition of being proper over the base, by way of a cited lemma, gives that the projections from these base changes to the members of the covering are proper (proof lines 6739-6743). Properness of the morphism from Z to the base then descends by the earlier lemma on descending properness, and the conclusion for the closed subset follows from the definition (proof lines 6744-6746). The claim is H2: the reduction from a closed subset to its reduced induced scheme structure is a real step, the identification of the base changes has to be made, and the descent lemma is then applied to the resulting morphisms.
